projects.title: The Univer-City

The idea of universe-city aim to break the imagining frontier between those two entities, it makes of the university an open space, with multiple sources. In our vision of the territory, it make sense to see Brussel as a complex web, where the universe-cities has an important role. The pole solbosh play his part in it. We highlighted 5 main aspects of the Solbosch campus and its surrounding at the scale of the Brussels University District. Linking the campus to the city, mobility systems , the landscape design, the environmental developments (including water management, and energy) and the notion of harmonism, in broad aspects, are the main point of concerns. These strategies not only help us to discuss sustainability beyond the environmental issues, but the social and economical levels are also taken into account. Through connecting the university with the city of Brussel, the campus will be transformed into open space for the neighborhood. Our first ambition is to open the campus to the city. projects.title: Bending-active responsive grid shell
projects.description:
The project is an attempt to combine bending-active structural elements in a responsive system. The pavilion consists of a grid-shell that can be controlled with set of wires. The wires can be separately tensioned by the users according to different needs and weather. The aims of the project is to enrich the connection between Brussels locals and the outdoor spaces. Giving the opportunity to the users to alter and shape the pavilion. The seven tensioned wires of the pavilion shape tens of alternatives. 

 Temporary structures are everywhere. They define the outdoor spaces and fill the void between permanent constructions. They follow the organic evolution of citiesâ€™ needs and daily functions. Such organic development should be backed by transformable systems that provide flexibility. Transformable structure systems change from one state to another. They can be rapidly assembled and disassembled, then transported to another place to reuse the same materials and reduce the amount of waste.
projects.role: Design, Research, structural analysis, parametric modeling

projects.title: The Chavilion: Scissor chair-pavilion
projects.description:
The Chavilion is a design project to create an indoor pavilion for the architectural atelier at VUB. The pavilion is a kit of parts system consists of a main repetitive unit. The system is intended to work as a Lego to assure transformability. The main block in the system is a stand-alone functional chair with scissor deplorability. Fixing 6-8 chairs together creates the arch of the pavilion that is still deployable. 

 The project included a structural analysis using â€œKaramba3Dâ€ plugin on grasshopper, it also included creating a 1/5 scaled scissor system to test the whole project functionality. The chair utilized the scissor system to provide 5 different shapes of uses.

projects.title: ULB timber tower: timber is the new concrete
projects.description: The ULB Timber Tower is part of a master plan to develop the ULB campus in Brussels, Belgium. The project proposes an entrance building that directly welcomes visitors and students arriving along the campus's main axis. The aims of the ULB Timber Tower reflect the vision of the master plan while pursuing four main goals: 1) to promote sustainability and lead the community by example; 2) to establish a symbolic identity for the university; 3) to strengthen the connection between the city and the university; and 4) to provide the functional spaces needed to accommodate the constant increase in students and expand university capacity.

projects.title: Bending-active plate components in configurable kit-of-pats systems
projects.description: This research investigates transformable wooden kit-of-parts systems through digital and physical modeling. It conceptualizes the structure as an assembly of modular components constructed on site and proposes a reconfigurable temporary system capable of adapting to different shapes and sizes using a consistent set of elements. A systematic method for connecting components is introduced, based on joints arranged within symmetrical grids and solids. Each face is replaced by a modular element, with pairs of elements connected through a single joint. The resulting structural configurations are derived from thoroughly studied polyhedral geometries or tessellations. The regularity of these systems is key to their reconfigurability.

projects.title: First permanent moon base
projects.description:
The spacefaring age promises immense potential, offering humanity access to vast resources, materials, and energy beyond Earth. In 2004, George W. Bush introduced a vision for renewed lunar exploration through a series of robotic missions designed to gather data on lunar resources and identify suitable construction sites for future habitation.

This project presents a vision, conceived in 2014, of an early step toward the colonization of the Moon. It explores the development of an initial unmanned lunar base as the foundation for a permanent human presence.

The first permanent Moon base represents a critical milestone in the transition to a new era of exploration. It will enable deeper access to the solar system, support the establishment of extraterrestrial settlements, and shift humanityâ€™s perspective from a â€œclosed Earthâ€ mindset to a broader, open-space vision of progress and discovery.

projects.title: ReciPlyDome
projects.description:
In the event sector, where there is a search for architectural constructions with an innovative morphology, reuse is key to strive towards more sustainable events. Designing modular structures and detailing them for easy disassembly and re-assembly is an ideal way to encourage and facilitate reuse. This way a longer lifespan is assured for the used components. However, temporary (event) structures are often hard to assemble, which can compromise their reusability. The difficulties of assembly are usually induced by the morphology of the modules or by using certain types of connections. Therefore these structures require optimization in terms of assembly while remaining resource efficient.

The main objective of this research is to reimagine a developed structure, the ReciPlyDome, and optimize it in terms of assembly. The ReciPlyDome is a reciprocal dome structure based on a rhombic triacontahedron, whereby all elements are identical (except for the five elements that touch the ground). During the assembly phase of the first version of the ReciPlyDome, torsion in the components appeared to hinder efficient construction. To eliminate this, the dome was reviewed, which led to the development of a new connection system and an improved shape for the beams. A new full-scale version of the dome has been built, showing the positive effect of the improved connector system and the optimized beam position. In-situ measurements were made after construction, illustrating good correspondence between the digital and built model. Further research will focus on the covering of this modular reciprocal dome for outdoor use.
projects.role: Technical optimisation, modelings, cover design, research, constructions.

projects.title: Integration of rigid plates in deployable scissor structures
projects.description: This research investigates two geometric approaches for integrating rigid plates into deployable scissor structures, aiming to overcome the limitations of flexible membrane coverings in temporary architectural applications. Scissor grids are well known for their rapid deployability and compact storage, yet their broader application has been constrained by coverings that contribute little to structural capacity and often lack durability. To address this limitation, two novel strategies are proposed in this research: (i) extrusion-surfaced plates embedded within uniaxially transforming planar scissor structures, and (ii) hyperbolic ruled surface plates incorporated into three-dimensional scissor modules. The study combines the automation process of geometric modeling, deployment constraint analysis, and joint optimization to examine the feasibility and implications of these hybrid systems. Results indicate that rigid plate integration expands the range of spatial configurations achievable with scissor grids and improves their functional potential. By advancing design methodologies for hybrid deployable systems, this work contributes to the development of more robust, reconfigurable, and efficient solutions for temporary spatial applications.
projects.subtitle: geometrical modelling and design by prototyping
